I'm a retired LEO and was a state certified evidence technician; I did the work for 7 years processing over 2500 crime scenes. I've gone through scores and scores of sites that posted alleged Sandy Hook photos and have yet to see evidence that 26 people were slaughtered. Perhaps the media filtered out the worst bloody scenes, but I have problems accepting the official story. Here's why:

1) No medical waste. Ambulance crews were dispatched and EMT's responded, yet I have yet to see even a single 4X4 gauze pad wrapper in any photo. Nothing that would indicate that emergency medical treatment was provided or even contemplated. I guess none of the EMT's thought that they wanted to do anything helpful?

2) Blood tracks. I have processed scenes where the pool of blood from a stabbing victim was so thick I had to hold onto to kitchen countertops so my boots wouldn't slide, loose my balance and land me in the mess. Did every responder float through this bloody mess? Good heavens, the school hallways where all these EMTs and cops had to traipse from room to room were spotless!

3) High velocity blood spatters. My training included blood fluid evidence collection. I have yet to see a single high velocity blood spatter. Medium velocity spatters are where you can see the drops of blood on the walls, ceiling or floor. High velocity spatters are more like a mist. With head shots there (usually) can be bits of hair, bone and brains distributed through the spatter. The victim's clothing can hinder the spatter display as well as the victim's distance from an object that would intercept the spatter. But there's just nothing for me to hang a massacre hat on.
